author: implementation-agent

findings.summary: Reader facsimile asset URL encoding reimplements the RFC3986 segment policy locally.
findings.consequence: Future changes to path segment escaping can drift between facsimile asset URLs, manifest request serialization, resolver canonical paths, and app navigation. The current manifest validator prevents unsafe Reader work IDs before this helper is used, so this is a maintainability risk rather than a confirmed runtime defect.
findings.evidence: The owned helper at line 210 wraps encodeURIComponent and re-escapes [!'()*]. Equivalent encoders exist in app/lib/internal-navigation.ts, server/utils/work-manifest-client.ts, server/api/reader/resolve/[author]/[title].get.ts, server/api/reader/resolve/[author]/[title]/[mediatype].get.ts, and server/utils/author-document.ts; architecture-policy coverage currently enforces shared use for selected app routes but not this private facsimile asset encoder.
findings.recommendation: Move the RFC3986 segment encoder behind one shared app/server-safe URL utility and import it here for facsimileImageUrl, while keeping manifest validation as the source authority for allowed Reader work IDs.
